texts.summary: Duquesne discusses negotiations with the Tripolins, the return of enslaved French subjects and captured ships, vessels suitable for use as fire-ships, treaty provisions and naval affairs. The later letter states the obligation to retain the position until express orders arrive and the hope of ending the campaign advantageously. (Abraham Duquesne to Seignelay, 25 September 1681; later letter in the same September correspondence, as given in George Lasry's report.)
texts.note: Excerpts only: lasry_entry.md holds George Lasry's report entry (metadata, excerpts of the decipherment, translation). His full transcription of the ciphertext and his full decryption (BnF cipher research, 10 Oct 2026) are not in the repository: needs contributor, George Lasry. The contemporary interlinear decipherment on the leaves is on the Gallica images only, not transcribed here.
